quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Titles of works take a singular verb, even when they contain plural nouns
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Great Expectations ___ one of Dickens's most famous novels.
quests.completedSentence: Great Expectations is one of Dickens's most famous novels.
quests.grammarRule: Titles of works take a singular verb, even when they contain plural nouns
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Great Expectations' is the title of one novel, so it takes a singular verb: 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: A book title names one single work, no matter how many words or names appear in it.
quests.example: Great Expectations is one of Dickens's most famous novels.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Titles of works take a singular verb, even when they contain plural nouns
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Little Women ___ the story of four sisters growing up in New England.
quests.completedSentence: Little Women tells the story of four sisters growing up in New England.
quests.grammarRule: Titles of works take a singular verb, even when they contain plural nouns
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Little Women' is one title, so the verb takes -s: 'tells'.
quests.nativeTip: Even though the title mentions four sisters, the title itself is one single book.
quests.example: Little Women tells the story of four sisters growing up in New England.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Titles of works take a singular verb, even when they contain plural nouns

quests.ruleExplanation: 'The Canterbury Tales' is the name of one book, so it takes a singular verb: 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: This title includes the word 'Tales' (plural), but the book itself is still one single work.
quests.example: The Canterbury Tales is a collection of stories told by pilgrims.
